lesson_title: Voices and Pictures Through the Air
hook_text: South Africa got television only in 1976, more than forty years after people in Britain first watched it.
clip_script: Newcastle, in KwaZulu-Natal. Grandpa turns the dial of an old radio, and a voice crackles out, reading the news in isiZulu. He remembers the 5th of January 1976, when the whole street crowded into one house to watch the first television broadcast in South Africa, on a small black-and-white screen. Today, Musa watches cartoons on a big flat screen and streams music on a phone. Voices and pictures, carried through the air, to millions at once.
visual_style: Whiteboard of radio waves spreading from a tall mast to an old radio, a black-and-white TV, a satellite dish and a phone, with the years 1923, 1936, 1976 and today along a timeline.
mood: Nostalgic and amazed, like hearing grandparents' stories.
pacing: Slow, crackly radio start, a burst of excitement for the first TV night, then fast modern screens.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and ask an older person what they remember about the first TV in South Africa.
